verdict: HII had a record quarter: revenue rose 11% to $3.5 billion, profit jumped 50%, and $32.4 billion of new Navy awards locked in most shipbuilding revenue through 2030.

segments.name: Newport News Shipbuilding
segments.note: Aircraft carriers and submarines built in Virginia — the biggest yard, and the growth engine this quarter on higher submarine and carrier volumes.

segments.name: Ingalls Shipbuilding
segments.note: Destroyers and amphibious ships built in Mississippi; growth came from amphibious assault ship volumes.

segments.name: Mission Technologies
segments.note: Defense technology, unmanned sea vehicles and services. Reported sales were $792M before $41M of sales between HII's own segments are removed.

opex.name: General & administrative (net)
opex.note: Running the company: $257M of general and administrative costs, partly offset by $26M of income from operating investments, less $3M of other losses.

otherDetail: Non-operating retirement benefit income of $53M and $2M of other income, less $26M of interest expense — net $29M.

takeaways.title: A mountain of new orders
takeaways.text: New contract awards of $32.4 billion in one quarter — including Block VI Virginia-class and Build II Columbia-class submarine contracts — have secured about 90% of expected shipbuilding revenue through 2030.

takeaways.title: Newport News is carrying growth
takeaways.text: Newport News Shipbuilding revenue rose 18% to $1.9 billion on submarine and aircraft-carrier work, and its segment profit jumped 65% on contract adjustments and incentives in the Virginia-class program.

takeaways.title: Cash flow caught up
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $429 million, versus just $16 million a year ago, as operating cash flow more than quadrupled to $520 million. Profit growth is finally showing up as cash.
